title: Engineer III Generation Interconnection
description:
Location: Carmel, IN; Eagan, MN; or Little Rock, AR

As a **Engineer III – Generator Interconnection**, you’ll play a role in evaluating new and changing generation across the MISO footprint. You’ll assist with power system studies that help determine how generation can reliably interconnect to the transmission system while serving as a technical resource for MISO’s interconnection customers, Transmission Owners, and neighboring RTOs.

This role combines technical power system analysis, problem-solving, and customer interaction. Depending on your assignments, you may help coordinate studies from kickoff through completion and keeping multiple stakeholders aligned along the way.

**How You’ll Make an Impact**

In this role, you will:

* Assist with system impact studies for generator interconnection requests in MISO’s Generator Interconnection Queue, evaluating the reliability impacts of connecting new resources to the transmission system.
* Review projects proposed by MISO’s Transmission Owners, providing technical recommendations based on power system analysis and established reliability requirements.
* Assist with assigned projects, communicating study results, technical requirements, and project details to interconnection customers, Transmission Owners, neighboring RTOs, and internal teams.

**What Makes This Role Exciting**

Generator interconnection is at the center of a rapidly changing electric grid. In this role, your studies won’t simply live in a report—they’ll help determine how new generation projects move forward, what transmission improvements may be needed, and how MISO continues to maintain a reliable system as the generation fleet evolves.

You’ll have the opportunity to build deep technical expertise while gaining exposure to customers, Transmission Owners, neighboring grid operators, and teams across MISO. title: EPC Project Manager
description:
**EPC Project Manager**

**Position Summary**

The EPC Project Manager is responsible for the successful execution of Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) of substation and transmission projects from project award through commissioning and closeout. This position provides leadership and direction for all aspects of project delivery, including safety, engineering coordination, procurement, construction management, financial performance, scheduling, quality assurance, customer relations, and risk management.

The Project Manager serves as the primary point of contact for utility customers, engineering firms, vendors, subcontractors, and internal stakeholders. The role is accountable for delivering projects safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with contractual requirements while maintaining exceptional customer satisfaction.

Projects may include greenfield and brownfield substations, station expansions, rebuilds, breaker replacements, transformer installations, protection and control upgrades, transmission interconnections, and utility infrastructure projects ranging from distribution voltage through EHV systems.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

**Project Leadership**

* Lead EPC substation projects from conceptual development through commissioning and turnover.
* Develop and maintain comprehensive project execution plans.
* Establish project objectives, budgets, schedules, and performance metrics.
* Coordinate engineering, procurement, construction, and commissioning activities.
* Provide leadership to Project Engineers, Construction Managers, Superintendents, Schedulers, and Project Controls personnel.
* Foster a culture focused on safety, quality, accountability, teamwork, and operational excellence.
